notes: Daxi culture of the Three Gorges; the page and infobox give '5000-3300 BC', 'centered in the Three Gorges region around the middle Yangtze', 'ranged from western Hubei to eastern Sichuan and the Pearl River Delta'; type site Daxi 'in the Qutang Gorge around Wushan, Chongqing' (Nels Nelson, 1920s). Extent: a 110 km disc around Yichang (western Hubei) plus Chongqing (the page's eastern Sichuan) are drawn, confidence 2; the 'Pearl River Delta' of the page (a long way from the Three Gorges, with no site named) and the Hunan sites (Hunan appears on the page only in a genetics passage) are not drawn. The page gives no phases, no area and no predecessor ('Preceded by' empty). Successor: 'The Daxi culture was followed by the Qujialing culture'; the Qujialing page says its earliest evidence '(3400-3000 BC) may belong to the final phase of the Daxi culture', so the two overlap in time; the Qujialing dossier starts in the Jianghan Plain in 3400 and takes the Yichang disc in 3300. Chongqing passes to nobody (confidence 1: the Qujialing page does not reach Sichuan). Exchange with the Majiabang (white pan plates at the Majiabang type site) and jade influence from the delta are not territory. No area figure.
